metadata.description: Common issues and patterns for Workday Extend application development

patterns.description: Security policy changes are not enforced until explicitly activated
best_practices: Always run 'Activate Pending Security Policy Changes' after any security modification
Include security activation as a mandatory post-deployment step
Test security with the actual end-user accounts, not admin accounts
anti_patterns: Assuming security changes take effect immediately after saving
Testing only with admin accounts that bypass security restrictions

common_issues.description: Users report 'access denied' or cannot see app components after deployment, despite security groups being configured correctly
common_issues.solution: Run the task 'Activate Pending Security Policy Changes' in the tenant. Security changes remain in pending state until this task is executed.

patterns.description: Integration credentials (passwords, API keys, secrets) are not included in migration packages
best_practices: Maintain a secure credential inventory for each tenant
Include credential configuration as a mandatory post-migration checklist item
Document which integrations require credential re-entry
anti_patterns: Expecting credentials to transfer between tenants in migration packages
Storing credentials in business object data fields

common_issues.description: Integrations fail with authentication errors immediately after deploying to a new tenant
common_issues.solution: Re-enter all integration credentials (API keys, passwords, client secrets) in the target tenant. Credentials are intentionally excluded from migration packages for security reasons.

patterns.description: Workday IDs (WIDs) are unique per tenant and must not be hardcoded
best_practices: Use Reference IDs instead of WIDs when referencing Workday objects
Store tenant-specific values in a configuration business object
Use InstanceSearch components in the UI for user-driven object selection
anti_patterns: Hardcoding WID values in orchestrations or calculated fields
Assuming a WID from sandbox will work in production

common_issues.description: Orchestrations or calculated fields fail with 'instance not found' errors after deployment to a different tenant
common_issues.solution: Replace hardcoded WIDs with Reference IDs or configuration lookups. WIDs are generated per-tenant and will differ between sandbox, preview, and production.

patterns.description: Workday APIs do not support CORS, preventing direct browser-side API calls
best_practices: Always proxy Workday API calls through a backend server
Use server-side middleware (Lambda, Azure Functions, etc.) for API interactions
Within Extend apps, use orchestration integration steps for external calls
anti_patterns: Attempting to call Workday APIs directly from client-side JavaScript
Building SPAs that directly consume Workday REST endpoints

common_issues.description: Browser console shows CORS errors when attempting to call Workday APIs from a web application
common_issues.solution: Workday APIs do not include CORS headers. Route all API calls through a backend proxy server. Within Extend apps, use orchestration integration steps instead of client-side calls.

patterns.description: OAuth 2.0 refresh tokens are single-use; each refresh returns a new refresh token
best_practices: Always store the latest refresh token after each token refresh
Implement atomic token storage to prevent race conditions
Handle the 'invalid_grant' error by re-authenticating from scratch
anti_patterns: Reusing a refresh token after it has been exchanged
Having multiple processes share and simultaneously refresh the same token

common_issues.solution: Refresh tokens are single-use. If the new refresh token was not saved after the last refresh, you must re-authenticate. Also, refresh tokens expire after 14 days of inactivity. Implement proper token storage that saves the new refresh token atomically after each use.

patterns.description: Migration IDs are the cross-tenant identity for objects and must remain stable
best_practices: Assign meaningful migration IDs to all custom objects at creation time
Never change a migration ID after initial deployment to any non-sandbox tenant
Document migration IDs in your version control alongside changelogs
anti_patterns: Relying on auto-generated migration IDs
Changing migration IDs between deployments

common_issues.description: Migration import fails with 'duplicate migration ID' or creates duplicate objects instead of updating existing ones
common_issues.solution: Migration IDs must be stable and unique. If IDs were changed, Workday sees the object as new and creates a duplicate. Resolve by either reverting the migration ID or manually removing the duplicate in the target tenant.

patterns.description: Scheduled orchestration triggers are not included in migration packages
best_practices: Document all scheduled triggers as part of deployment runbook
Include schedule configuration as a post-deployment checklist item
Verify scheduled triggers are running after deployment
anti_patterns: Assuming scheduled triggers transfer with the orchestration definition

common_issues.description: Scheduled orchestrations work in sandbox but do not execute in the target tenant after migration
common_issues.solution: Schedules are not part of migration packages. Manually recreate the schedule trigger in the target tenant after import.

patterns.description: Workday APIs enforce rate limits that must be handled gracefully
best_practices: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries
Respect the Retry-After header in 429 responses
Use pagination with reasonable page sizes (100-200 records)
Cache API responses where data freshness allows
Schedule intensive operations during off-peak hours
anti_patterns: Ignoring 429 responses and retrying immediately
Making unbounded concurrent API calls
Polling APIs for changes instead of using events/notifications

common_issues.description: Integration fails intermittently with 429 errors, especially during batch operations
common_issues.solution: Implement exponential backoff: wait 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s between retries. Respect the Retry-After header. Reduce concurrent connections. Consider using bulk/batch API operations instead of individual calls.

patterns.description: Workday Extend has no built-in automated testing framework
best_practices: Maintain a structured test case document with test IDs, steps, and expected results
Test with multiple user roles (admin, manager, user, no-access) for every feature
Automate API-level testing with Postman/Newman for custom endpoints
Execute full regression before each deployment and after each Workday release
anti_patterns: Skipping testing because 'it worked in sandbox'
Testing only the happy path without negative test cases
Deploying to production without testing in preview tenant first

common_issues.description: Extend app breaks after a Workday biannual release
common_issues.solution: Always test your Extend app in the preview tenant 4 weeks before each production release. Watch for deprecated APIs, changed validation rules, and UI component updates.

patterns.description: Workday Expression Language (WEL) has significant limitations compared to general-purpose languages
best_practices: Keep WEL expressions simple and shallow (avoid nesting beyond 10 levels)
Use the 'Test Calculated Field' task to debug expressions interactively
Break complex logic into multiple simpler calculated fields
Store computed values in business object fields when the expression is performance-intensive
anti_patterns: Trying to implement loops or iteration in WEL (use collection functions instead)
Building deeply nested expressions that are hard to debug
Using WEL for logic that should be in an orchestration

common_issues.description: Calculated field returns an error about exceeding complexity limits
common_issues.solution: Break the expression into multiple smaller calculated fields that reference each other. WEL has a nesting depth limit of approximately 10-15 levels.
